topics.flagship-ru-ua: One report, carried by 5 outlets, says Ukraine's seven-stage attack caused major damage to the Crimean Bridge, a key symbol of Russia's occupation. Separately, the UK is reportedly supplying more than 1,000 air defence missiles as part of £240 million in winter support. A UN monitoring mission reported 372 civilians killed and 1,981 injured in October, 95% more than in October 2025, and Ukrainian authorities said 72 people died in a 2 November strike on a school shelter in Komyshuvakha.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Trump warned Iran after a CNN report that it was planning an attack, described as a 'dirty bomb' plot, against Washington, DC. Senior officials are reportedly relocating to military housing, and the story is carried by 14 outlets. Separately, a two-month lull reportedly ended with Iran's third strike on US targets in Bahrain, after the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group arrived in the region. Other items include analysis of a possible 'frozen conflict', a Houthi advance toward Aden, and an LPG tanker sinking off Bulgaria near where another ship went down after a drone attack the day before.
topics.T15: The stories are scattered local weather and preparedness items with no single major event. They include Cyclone Akvan preparations in Koraput, India, evacuation alerts lifted in Pemberton Valley after flooding, storm repair costs in Long Beach, and large waves closing California piers.
topics.T01: The Sudanese army reportedly carried out an air attack in West Kordofan that killed 13 people, including women and children, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers (3 outlets). Separately, an RSF field commander reportedly defected to the army and accused the UAE of financing the war. The remaining items are regional commentary and summit coverage on the East Asia Summit and ASEAN.
topics.T02: The stories are too sparse and generic to summarize meaningfully. They include a celebrity donation for winter shelter kits for displaced families in Gaza and a research study on displacement and childhood vaccination coverage.
topics.T04: Two people died in a Legionnaires' disease outbreak in South Yorkshire, UK, and the source is unidentified (3 outlets). PAHO says the US has officially lost its measles elimination status. Venezuela declared a national rabies quarantine after six deaths, and one outlet reports that Ebola has killed more than 5,000 people in the DRC, with treatment center staff unpaid for four months.
topics.T05: Turkish authorities raided the Istanbul offices of opposition channel Sozcu TV, halted its broadcasts and appointed a trustee, in what is described as another crackdown on pro-opposition television (3 outlets). The European Court of Human Rights called for the release of jailed lawmaker Can Atalay. Other items cover Bangladesh's NCP seeking a terrorist designation for the Awami League and Myanmar's parliamentary session ending.
topics.T06: A Dhaka court placed former DSCC mayor Sayeed Khokon on seven-day remand over a teenager's killing during the July uprising. Elsewhere, about 20,000 people marched in Athens for the 1973 uprising anniversary, with clashes and 15 detentions afterward. Over 100 people were arrested after the Dublin riots, French strike turnout reportedly fell ahead of Europe-wide protests, and Czech and Zimbabwean protest stories appear with little sourcing.
topics.T07: One outlet reports the US is preparing to test a nuclear-capable missile. Most coverage concerns the planned first Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, where nuclear arms, Ukraine, Iran and trade are expected on the agenda. A WSJ editorial warned that allies fear concessions and that the meeting could resemble a 'second Yalta'.
topics.T08: A terrorist was killed in an encounter in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir, with another reportedly trapped, following an attack in which three CRPF personnel were injured (6 outlets). Other items include a motorcycle IED that injured four in Khyber, Pakistan, US intelligence support for Nigeria's offensive, and arrests or detentions in Spain, Finland and North Macedonia over alleged attack plans.
topics.T09: One report says Aleksandr Antonov, a 66-year-old Santa Barbara man, has been imprisoned in Russia since March 2025. Rep. Salud Carbajal met his family to advocate for his release.
topics.T10: Coverage centers on defense budgets and procurement. Trump seeks a $1.5 trillion defense budget, but analysis says the midterms have likely doomed it, and Germany is spending a record €125 billion. Other items include a Quad leaders' meeting, Army efforts to bring private tech onto ranges, EU defense funding and Norwegian funding for nuclear-propulsion ship research.
topics.T11: Trump announced a new Quad military exercise after a summit with Japan, India and Australia in the Philippines (4 outlets). India's INS Sahyadri took part in the JAIMEX 2026 exercise with Japan. Experts warn China's Taiwan strategy blurs the line between exercises and war preparation, and a Mitchell Institute analysis reportedly found nearly 300 Chinese warplanes at 11 bases.
topics.T12: The NSA's internal classified network reportedly went down, according to CNN, with officials finding no evidence of a cyberattack (5 outlets). This came amid a string of US tech and banking outages, including at Charles Schwab. Rubio said there is zero evidence linking the outages to hackers or foreign states, DHS Secretary Mullin attributed them to 'superintelligence' stressing older systems, and one outlet reports a separate cyberattack on 178 major companies.
topics.T13: The stories are disparate and not part of one clear event. They include commentary on Ceuta and EU migration policy, VOX leader Abascal's claim that 11,000 migrants reached the Canary Islands, and a Nigerian House call to act on Gabon demolitions displacing Nigerians.
topics.T14: A single report says the US Embassy in Madrid urged Americans traveling in Europe over the holiday season to stay vigilant in crowded places, citing possible threats from terrorist groups and criminals. It also flagged strikes and demonstrations.
topics.T16: Israeli media reports allege interference by Netanyahu's office on Election Day (2 outlets), and Likud is seeking an extra week to appeal results over alleged violations. Haaretz found most of its complaints did not concern matters that could affect voting. Other items include New Zealand's post-election coalition talks and MMP concerns, Serbia's Students' List taking seats, and a Brazilian police probe of a Vance-linked donor network.

bluf: President Trump warned Iran of unprecedented retaliation after a CNN report that Tehran was working on plans, described as a 'dirty bomb' threat, to attack Washington, DC. This was the most widely carried story today (14 outlets), and senior officials are reportedly relocating to military housing. Ukraine reportedly carried out a seven-stage attack that caused major damage to the Crimean Bridge, a key symbol of Russia's occupation, according to 5 outlets. The Sudanese army reportedly carried out an air strike in West Kordofan that killed 13 people, including women and children, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. In Jammu and Kashmir, one terrorist was killed and another reportedly trapped in a Kulgam encounter, following an attack last week in which three CRPF personnel were injured. An LPG tanker sank off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, according to the Bulgarian defense ministry, a few dozen miles from where another ship went down after a drone attack the day before. One outlet also reports that a two-month lull ended with Iran's third strike on US targets in Bahrain, shortly after the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group arrived in the region. Trump, Xi and Putin are also due to hold their first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, with nuclear arms, Ukraine and Iran expected on the agenda and allies reportedly anxious about possible concessions.
